::: {.page-lede}
My teaching goal is to help students move from applying statistical procedures to making **defensible research decisions**. I organize quantitative instruction around the full research process: question, design, measurement, model choice, diagnostics, uncertainty, interpretation, and reproducible communication.
:::

## Teaching Philosophy

Effective quantitative work combines technical execution with judgment about what a design and dataset can support. Software and formulas matter, but I embed them within a broader sequence of inquiry: define the research question, understand the data structure, choose a model the data can support, examine assumptions and diagnostics, interpret uncertainty, and communicate conclusions responsibly.

### Research Methods Mentoring

I mentor graduate students and research trainees on study design, measurement, analysis planning, model selection, diagnostics, interpretation, and reproducible documentation. My mentoring approach gradually shifts responsibility to the student as they gain methodological independence.

## Teaching Approach

### Authentic Inquiry
I use real research problems to connect statistical technique with substantive reasoning. Code is a tool for quantitative thinking, not an end in itself.

### Scaffolding and Feedback
Students enter methods courses with different levels of statistical preparation and programming experience. I use conceptual explanations, worked examples, annotated code, structured decision prompts, and iterative feedback while maintaining common expectations for methodological reasoning.

### Reproducible Practice
Students should leave a methods course able to produce an analysis that another researcher can understand, reproduce, and critique. I emphasize transparent workflows, diagnostic checks, and clear reporting of assumptions and uncertainty.
